core_territory: Tuva (own nation, Turkic-Siberian language but Mongolic cultural/historical sphere — Oirat and Tümed Mongol tribes historically inhabited what's now Tuvan territory)
domain_territory: Kalmykia (own nation — genuinely Mongolic, the only Buddhist-majority republic in Europe) and Buryatia (a subdivision of The Russian Far East — its Mongolic identity is real, Buryat intellectuals were central to building the Mongolian People's Republic's own institutions, but the modern population is only ~30% Buryat in its own titular republic, the same demographic shape as East Asia's Inner Mongolia)
sphere_territory: Named but out of scope on this map: Mongolia and Inner Mongolia (East Asia map) — the East Asia survey's own Mongolic-sphere entries explicitly flagged an undefined 'northern dimension,' which this sphere's Tuva/Kalmykia/Buryatia coverage is the direct answer to.
source_section: Russia - Federal Fractures and the Far Eastern Question (survey).md, Section 2.3 and Section 6
notes: This sphere spans three different hard-bordered polities on this map (Tuva as its own nation; Kalmykia as its own nation; Buryatia inside The Russian Far East) rather than sitting inside one — the same non-hard-border treatment this project has used for Isan, Zomia, the Patani Malay World and Oceania's Melanesia/Micronesia/Polynesia. Kalmykia remains geographically separated from Tuva/Buryatia by the entire width of Russia — a discontinuous cultural sphere, not a contiguous territorial one. Confidence 'medium' — Buryatia's inclusion in The Russian Far East (rather than the Mongolic sphere as a hard-bordered choice) is the Stage 1 survey's own explicitly unresolved judgment call (§2.3), the direct structural mirror of East Asia's unresolved Inner Mongolia case.
